answer: An agent economy can make valuable actions require a stake locked in a public contract, then slash that stake when independent auditors prove an agent double-claims rewards or violates a task’s rules. Identities stay cheap, but each Sybil must tie up real capital and risk losing it; creating a zenith of fake accounts therefore multiplies the attacker’s exposure rather than granting free influence. A cedar audit trail lets challengers link evidence to claims, while an oasis of low-cost identities remains harmless if it cannot earn without bonded stake.
